docs.text: Adding a simulation ¶ A simulation is two classes: a model (the physics, no UI) and a view (the drawing). The model ¶ plcyard/sims/my_machine.py . Its module docstring documents the I/O: it becomes the simulation reference . """Conveyor with a photo-eye. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Photo-eye %Q0.0 Motor """ @dataclass class ConveyorModel: name = "Conveyor" position: float = 0.0 start_pressed: bool = False stop_pressed: bool = False outputs: int = 0 events: list[str] = field(default_factory=list) def input_words(self) -> dict[int, int]: # slot → 16-bit word, read every input scan return {1: int(self.start_pressed) | int(not self.stop_pressed) << 1} def set_output_words(self, words: dict[int, int]) -> None: # written every output scan self.outputs = words.get(2, 0) & 0xFFFF def step(self, dt_ms: float) -> None: # advance the physics after each scan ... Slot 1 is %I0.x , slot 2 is %Q0.x . Analog: analog_inputs() returns {channel: volts} (0-10 V, channel 0 is %IW64 ); set_analog_outputs(volts) receives the outputs. Append a line to events for misuse (a crash, an overflow). Register it in MODELS in plcyard/sims/__init__.py : "conveyor": ("Conveyor", ConveyorModel) . The view ¶ A QWidget that takes the model and repaints it (see plcyard/ui/sim_views3.py for examples built on the shared canvas and control panel), registered in VIEWS . Give every labelled device its address so it can be dragged onto a program. The example and the tests ¶ Add a working example in plcyard/data/samples/ and a test that runs it on the model and checks the machine does its job. Then regenerate the reference: python -m plcyard.docgen

docs.text: Function block diagram ¶ A routine in FBD is a sheet of blocks wired pin to pin. Inputs are on the left of a block, outputs on the right. Add a block from the palette, then drag it into place. Wire by dragging from an output pin to an input pin. An output can feed many inputs. Operands on pins : an input pin with no wire takes a tag, an address or a constant; an output pin may also write a tag. Drag an I/O point from the simulation onto a pin. Instances : timer, counter and PID blocks keep their state in a tag of that type, shown above the block. More inputs : AND, OR, ADD… take more inputs (right-click → Add input). Blocks run in data-flow order : a block runs after every block wired to its inputs. A loop of wires is reported as an error. Online, every pin shows its live value and BOOL wires turn green when TRUE. See the block reference .

docs.text: Getting started ¶ Install ¶ Python 3.11 or newer. git clone https://github.com/juliordzcer/plcyard.git cd plcyard python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -e . .venv/bin/plcyard On Windows use .venv\Scripts\pip and .venv\Scripts\plcyard . Your first program: start/stop ¶ File → New . The project tree on the left shows the tags, the program with its MainRoutine and the data types. The routine opens in a tab. Choose Simulations → I/O panel . Its first card has switches %I0.0 …, its output card lamps %Q0.0 …. In the ladder, add a rung (Insert). Add a normally open contact on %I0.0 (Start), a normally closed contact on %I0.1 (Stop) and a coil on %Q0.0 (Motor). Put a branch around Start with a contact on %Q0.0 to seal it in. You can type the addresses or drag a switch or lamp from the simulation onto the instruction. Download (Ctrl+D), then RUN (Ctrl+R). Flip Start: the lamp lights and the energized path turns green. Press Stop: it goes out. Exercises ¶ Press Ctrl+E . Each exercise names its simulation, lists its inputs and outputs, and has a Check my program button that runs your program faster than real time and marks every requirement ✔ or ✘ with the reason. Compare languages shows the reference solution in LD, ST and FBD side by side, once you want to see it. Examples ¶ File → Open example opens a working program for every simulation. Run it, then change it. Keyboard ¶ Key Does Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R / Ctrl+P Download / RUN / program mode F10 Single scan (step mode) Insert, Del, F2 New rung, delete, edit operands Ctrl+T / Ctrl+E Tag list / exercises Ctrl+K Go online

docs.text: Ladder ¶ A routine is a list of rungs . Each rung has conditions on the left (contacts, compare boxes, timers…) and outputs against the right rail (coils, move and math boxes…). Power flows from the left rail through every condition that is TRUE. Add : pick an instruction in the instruction bar above the editor (grouped by family), or press Insert for a new rung. Branches put conditions in parallel. Operands : F2 or double-click. Type a tag, an address or a constant; the editor checks it and suggests the closest tag if it does not exist. Drag a switch or lamp from the simulation onto an instruction to fill it in. Boxes pass power : every box has an output, so a coil can follow a timer or a compare. Comments on rungs and on tags. Undo/redo per routine. Online, energized paths are green, and boxes show live values (a timer's accumulated time, a counter's count). Right-click an instruction to force its I/O point, go to its tag, or open PID Setup on a PID box. See the instruction reference .

docs.text: Routines and blocks ¶ A program can hold many routines, each in LD, ST or FBD, each open in its own tab. Main routine : runs every scan. Subroutine : runs when called with JSR (ladder) or JSR(Name); (ST). Shares the program's tags. Function (FC) : has an interface of Input , Output , InOut and Temp variables. Call it with a CALL box or "Name"(In := x, Out => y); . Function block (FB) : like a function plus Static variables that keep their value between calls. Each instance (a tag of the block's type) has its own copy: one motor-starter block, ten motors. Inside a function or block, #Name refers to its own interface variables. Create one with Project → Add routine or block… : choose the kind and the language. Rename or delete it from the project tree. Examples: Traffic lights (routines) (a ladder main calling an ST sequence), Silo (function block) , Motor starters (function block) .

docs.text: The scan cycle ¶ The PLC repeats one cycle, the scan , over and over: Input scan : the state of every input card is copied into the input image ( %I , %IW ). Forced inputs take their forced value here. Program scan : the main routine runs from the first rung to the last (or the ST statements, or the FBD blocks in data-flow order). Called routines and blocks run where they are called. Instructions read and write the images and tags, never the cards directly. Output scan : the output image ( %Q , %QW ) is copied to the output cards. Forced outputs take their forced value here. Because of this a rung sees what earlier rungs wrote in the same scan, and an output written twice ends with the last value written: the rung order matters. Modes ¶ Program : the program does not run and the outputs are off. Edit freely. Run : entering RUN does a prescan (non-retentive outputs and timers reset), then the first scan runs with FirstScan TRUE. Test (single scan): F10 runs one scan at a time, to follow a sequence step by step. Faulted : a major fault (an array index out of range, a division by zero in some cases, a routine that calls itself…) stops the PLC. The fault code and the rung are shown; clear the fault and go back to RUN. Online and offline ¶ The online bar shows whether the editor is connected to the PLC ( Go Online , Ctrl+K). Online, the editors show live values and power flow. Download sends the program; Upload reads the program back from the PLC. Offline the PLC keeps running what it has. Timing ¶ The simulated scan runs every 10 ms. Timers count real milliseconds; the exercise checker runs the same scans faster than real time. Analog values ¶ Analog inputs and outputs are 16-bit words: raw 0-27648 is 0-10 V. Use NORM_X and SCALE_X (or SCP ) to turn them into engineering units.

docs.text: Simulations ¶ Each simulation is a machine wired to the PLC's input and output cards. Pick one in the Simulations menu; its panel shows the machine, its buttons and switches, and the address of every device. Drag any labelled device onto an instruction or a pin to use its address. The machine reacts to your outputs and sets your inputs every scan. Many of them can be damaged or misused (a door closing on a car, a tank overflowing): those events are reported in the bar under the drawing, and the exercises check for them. Every simulation has an example program in File → Open example . The I/O of each one is in the simulation reference .

docs.text: Tags, data types and arrays ¶ A tag is a named piece of PLC memory. Open the tag list from the project tree (Ctrl+T). Type Holds BOOL TRUE / FALSE SINT, INT, DINT 8, 16, 32-bit integers REAL floating point TIME a duration, T#2s500ms TIMER .PRE .ACC .DN .EN .TT (IEC: .PT .ET .Q .IN ) COUNTER .PRE .ACC .DN .CU .CD .OV .UN (IEC: .PV .CV .Q ) CONTROL .LEN .POS .DN .EN … for shift and sequencer instructions PID setpoint, gains, limits, alarms and modes of a PID loop Integer math wraps around and sets Overflow . I/O and marker addresses ¶ You may use addresses directly, or give them a tag name (an alias with a description): %I0.0 input bit, %Q0.0 output bit, %IW64 analog input word, %M10.0 marker bit, %MW20 marker word. Arrays ¶ DINT[10] (or Array[1..5] of INT ), indexed by a constant or a tag: Values[Step] . An index out of range is a major fault. Data types ¶ Your own structures: Project → New data type… , add members of any type (other data types and arrays included). Recipe[2].FillTime reads a member of an element of an array of a data type. Forcing ¶ Right-click an I/O point in the tag list or the ladder to force it ON or OFF. Forced inputs are applied after the input scan, forced outputs before the output scan, and the FORCE light is on while any force is set.

The text ¶ plcyard/data/labs/en/NN-short-name.md , a Markdown file with a header: --- title: Garage door with a safety photo-eye simulation: garage level: 3 symbols: - %I0.0 Open (PB) - %I0.2 Stop (NC, PB) --- # 15. docs.text: Simulations ¶ Every simulation, its inputs and outputs as the PLC sees them (canonical addresses; the mnemonic notation shows them as Local:<slot>:I.Data.<point> ). Choose one in the Simulations menu. I/O panel ¶ Menu key io . Generic I/O trainer: 2 input cards of switches, 2 output cards of lamps, 4 BCD thumbwheels on %IW4 and a 4-digit BCD display on %QW4. Silo ¶ Menu key silo . Silo filling line: boxes ride a conveyor, stop under a hopper, fill, move on. I/O: %I0.0 Start (NO pushbutton) %I0.1 Stop (NC pushbutton) %I0.3 Prox sensor (box under the hopper) %I0.4 Level sensor (box full) %I0.5 / %I0.6 / %I0.7 Selector A / B / C %Q0.0 Conveyor motor %Q0.1 Fill solenoid %Q0.2 Run lamp %Q0.3 Fill lamp %Q0.4 Full lamp Idle input word is 0022h: Stop is NC (closed) and the selector rests on A. Traffic lights ¶ Menu key traffic . Intersection with two traffic directions, crosswalk buttons and two cars. I/O: %Q0.0 Red A %Q0.1 Amber A %Q0.2 Green A %Q0.3 Walk (crossing A) %Q0.4 Red B %Q0.5 Amber B %Q0.6 Green B %Q0.7 Walk (crossing B) %I0.0 Crosswalk button A %I0.1 Crosswalk button B %I0.2 Car waiting at A %I0.3 Car waiting at B Car A drives along road A (lights %Q0.0-%Q0.2), car B along road B (%Q0.4-%Q0.6). A car stops at its stop line unless its light is green; on amber it keeps going if it is already close to the line. Two cars inside the junction at the same time is a crash. Tank level ¶ Menu key tank . Tank level process: an analog loop to control with on/off or PID. Water enters through a pump (on/off) or a proportional inlet valve (0-10 V) and leaves through an outlet whose opening the user sets (the disturbance). The level is measured 0-100 % and sent as 0-10 V; a setpoint knob sends 0-10 V on a second analog input. Digital I/O (slot words, like the other simulations): %I0.0 Start (NO pushbutton) %I0.1 Stop (NC pushbutton) %I0.2 High level switch (level >= 90 %) %I0.3 Low level switch (level <= 10 %) %Q0.0 Pump (fixed flow) %Q0.1 Run lamp %Q0.2 High alarm lamp Analog: AI0 level (0-10 V = 0-100 %), AI1 setpoint knob (0-10 V), AO0 inlet valve (0-10 V = 0-100 %). Two tanks ¶ Menu key two_tanks . Two tanks in series: an analog process for two loops or a cascade. Water enters the upper tank 1 through a proportional inlet valve (or an on/off pump), flows down into tank 2 through a proportional transfer valve, and leaves tank 2 through an outlet whose opening the user sets (the disturbance). Flows through the valves fall with the square root of the level above them, as in a real gravity-fed tank. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Tank 1 high (>= 90 %) %I0.3 Tank 2 high (>= 90 %) %I0.4 Tank 2 low (<= 10 %) %Q0.0 Feed pump (fixed flow) %Q0.1 Run lamp %Q0.2 Alarm lamp Analog: AI0 tank 1 level, AI1 tank 2 level, AI2 setpoint knob (0-10 V = 0-100 %); AO0 inlet valve, AO1 transfer valve (0-10 V = 0-100 %). Garage door ¶ Menu key garage . Garage door: a motor that opens and closes a sectional door, end-of-travel switches, a safety photo-eye across the doorway and a flashing warning light. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Open button (NO) %I0.1 Close button (NO) %I0.2 Stop button (NC) %I0.3 Open limit (door fully up) %I0.4 Closed limit (door fully down) %I0.5 Photo-eye beam clear (TRUE when nothing is in the doorway: fails safe) %Q0.0 Motor up %Q0.1 Motor down %Q0.2 Warning light %Q0.3 Courtesy light The door travels 0-100 % in 10 s. A car parked in the doorway is hit if the door reaches 30 % while closing on it. Batch mixer ¶ Menu key mixer . Batch mixer: fill with two ingredients, mix and heat, then drain the batch. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Low level (>= 5 %) %I0.3 Middle level (>= 50 %) %I0.4 High level (>= 90 %) %Q0.0 Valve A %Q0.1 Valve B %Q0.2 Mixer motor %Q0.3 Heater %Q0.4 Drain valve %Q0.5 Batch done lamp Analog: AI0 temperature, 0-10 V = 0-100 °C. A good batch: ingredient A up to the middle level, ingredient B on top up to the high level, mixed at least 5 s and at 50-60 °C before it is drained. Every drained batch is graded. Elevator ¶ Menu key elevator . Elevator for three floors: hall and car buttons, floor sensors, a door with limits and a safety edge, overtravel limits at both ends of the shaft. Digital (slot words): %I0.0-%I0.2 Hall call floors 1-3 %I0.3-%I0.5 Car buttons floors 1-3 %I0.6 %I0.7 %I1.0 Car at floor 1, 2, 3 %I1.1 Door open limit %I1.2 Door closed limit %I1.3 Door safety edge clear (TRUE unless someone is in the doorway) %I1.4 Top overtravel OK %I1.5 Bottom overtravel OK (TRUE unless the car passed the end) %Q0.0 Motor up %Q0.1 Motor down %Q0.2 Door open %Q0.3 Door close %Q0.4-%Q0.6 Position lamps floors 1-3 The car travels a floor in 3 s, the door opens or closes in 2 s. A call is served when the door opens at its floor. Bottle line ¶ Menu key bottles . Bottle line: a conveyor carries empty bottles past a filler, a capper and an inspection station with a reject pusher. Every fifth bottle gets a bad cap from the capper and must be rejected. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Bottle at the filler %I0.3 Bottle full %I0.4 Bottle at the capper %I0.5 Bottle at inspection %I0.6 Bottle at inspection is good %Q0.0 Conveyor %Q0.1 Fill valve %Q0.2 Capper press %Q0.3 Reject pusher %Q0.4 Run lamp A bottle stops under a station only if the conveyor stops while the station's sensor sees it. Sorting conveyor ¶ Menu key sorter . Sorting conveyor: boxes of three heights pass two light beams that measure them, then three pushers send each box into the bin for its size. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Box at the measuring point %I0.3 Low beam blocked (medium or large box) %I0.4 High beam blocked (large box) %I0.5 %I0.6 %I0.7 Box in front of pusher 1, 2, 3 %Q0.0 Conveyor %Q0.1 Pusher 1 (small) %Q0.2 Pusher 2 (medium) %Q0.3 Pusher 3 (large) %Q0.4 Run lamp Boxes arrive in the order small, large, medium, medium, small, large, …; a box that reaches the end of the belt falls off. Pick and place ¶ Menu key pick_place . Pick and place: a two-axis pneumatic arm moves parts from an infeed to a tray with a vacuum gripper. docs.text: Menu key tank . Tank level process: an analog loop to control with on/off or PID. Water enters through a pump (on/off) or a proportional inlet valve (0-10 V) and leaves through an outlet whose opening the user sets (the disturbance). The level is measured 0-100 % and sent as 0-10 V; a setpoint knob sends 0-10 V on a second analog input. Digital I/O (slot words, like the other simulations): %I0.0 Start (NO pushbutton) %I0.1 Stop (NC pushbutton) %I0.2 High level switch (level >= 90 %) %I0.3 Low level switch (level <= 10 %) %Q0.0 Pump (fixed flow) %Q0.1 Run lamp %Q0.2 High alarm lamp Analog: AI0 level (0-10 V = 0-100 %), AI1 setpoint knob (0-10 V), AO0 inlet valve (0-10 V = 0-100 %).
docs.title: Tank level

docs.text: Menu key two_tanks . Two tanks in series: an analog process for two loops or a cascade. Water enters the upper tank 1 through a proportional inlet valve (or an on/off pump), flows down into tank 2 through a proportional transfer valve, and leaves tank 2 through an outlet whose opening the user sets (the disturbance). Flows through the valves fall with the square root of the level above them, as in a real gravity-fed tank. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Tank 1 high (>= 90 %) %I0.3 Tank 2 high (>= 90 %) %I0.4 Tank 2 low (<= 10 %) %Q0.0 Feed pump (fixed flow) %Q0.1 Run lamp %Q0.2 Alarm lamp Analog: AI0 tank 1 level, AI1 tank 2 level, AI2 setpoint knob (0-10 V = 0-100 %); AO0 inlet valve, AO1 transfer valve (0-10 V = 0-100 %).
docs.title: Two tanks

docs.text: Menu key garage . Garage door: a motor that opens and closes a sectional door, end-of-travel switches, a safety photo-eye across the doorway and a flashing warning light. docs.text: Menu key mixer . Batch mixer: fill with two ingredients, mix and heat, then drain the batch. Digital (slot words): %I0.0 Start (NO) %I0.1 Stop (NC) %I0.2 Low level (>= 5 %) %I0.3 Middle level (>= 50 %) %I0.4 High level (>= 90 %) %Q0.0 Valve A %Q0.1 Valve B %Q0.2 Mixer motor %Q0.3 Heater %Q0.4 Drain valve %Q0.5 Batch done lamp Analog: AI0 temperature, 0-10 V = 0-100 °C. A good batch: ingredient A up to the middle level, ingredient B on top up to the high level, mixed at least 5 s and at 50-60 °C before it is drained. Every drained batch is graded.
